props.title: The Song of Bernadette
props.initialSlug: Peasant girl's divine visions shake a French town

sections.content: **The Song of Bernadette** (1943) stands as one of Hollywood's most compelling religious dramas, with Jennifer Jones delivering an Oscar-winning performance as Bernadette Soubirous, the French peasant girl who claimed to see visions of the Virgin Mary. The film expertly balances religious devotion with human skepticism, similar to how The Miracle of Our Lady of Fatima (1952) would later approach miraculous visions. Director Henry King creates an atmosphere of both mystical wonder and grounded realism, while cinematographer Arthur Miller's stunning black-and-white photography earned him an Academy Award.

sections.content: Religious cinema of the 1940s often tackled themes of faith versus doubt, with Going My Way (1944) and **The Keys of the Kingdom** (1944) exploring Catholic faith through more everyday circumstances. What sets **The Song of Bernadette** apart is its unflinching focus on miraculous events while maintaining dramatic tension through the opposition of secular authorities and skeptical clergy. Vincent Price delivers a nuanced performance as Imperial Prosecutor Dutour, representing rational skepticism without becoming a villain.

The film's influence on religious cinema cannot be overstated. Its respectful treatment of spiritual experiences influenced later works like The Nun's Story (1959) and **A Man Called Peter** (1955). Modern religious films like **The Passion of the Christ** (2004) owe a debt to Bernadette's approach to depicting divine experiences through a combination of restraint and powerful imagery. sections.content: **The Song of Bernadette** helped pave the way for the biblical epic boom of the 1950s and early 1960s. While not strictly a biblical story, its successful blend of spirituality and spectacle influenced films like **The Robe** (1953), **Ben-Hur** (1959), and **King of Kings** (1961). The film demonstrated that religious subjects could be both commercially successful and critically acclaimed when handled with artistic integrity.
